Use `snl entry references` to enumerate structured references to one Entry before rename, deletion, or dependency analysis.

### Availability
This Entry is a normative product contract. The command is implemented only when its canonical path appears in machine-readable `snl --help`; absence means planned and unavailable, never silently emulated through a different command.


### Command path
`entry/references` is the canonical transport-neutral command. The intended shell spelling is `snl entry references`. Current availability is advertised by machine-readable `snl --help`; an Agent/MCP adapter submits the same operation object instead of reconstructing shell text.

### Operation request
```json
{"protocol":"snl.operation/v1","command":"entry/references","root":"/absolute/workspace","arguments":{"id":"<exact-id>"}}
```
Every adapter accepts exactly this semantic request. Unknown argument keys are rejected. The CLI accepts `--root` and `--json` globally and emits one complete JSON document followed by a newline. Return an empty list as successful absence; do not conflate it with a missing queried identity.

### Success result
A successful call exits `0` and returns `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":true,"command":"entry/references","data":{},"diagnostics":[]}`. `data.items` is deterministically ordered and each occurrence includes owning entity/file plus a precise structured path or graph edge identity.

### Failure and exit semantics
Domain rejection (invalid data, not-found, conflict, or validation errors) exits `1`. Invocation, input I/O, unsupported workspace/schema, lock acquisition, and runtime failures exit `2`. Failure stdout under `--json` is exactly one `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":false,"command":"entry/references","error":{"code":"<stable-code>","message":"<actionable text>","details":{},"retryable":false}}`; no stack trace or prose contaminates stdout.

### State and concurrency
Read-only and stateless. Results are derived fresh from authoritative workspace data. Revisions, cursors, checked digests, and workspace revisions are opaque tokens. Repeated calls against unchanged bytes return equivalent semantic results.
